challengeFindings.title: An in-place run on dev whose tracked lock was dirty when the run started and is deleted during it now stops its bookkeeping commit with exit 10
A writer that re-creates a tracked lock between the deleted-file listing and the commit gets its live lock body committed as a modification
The pending climb test plants its decision file at logs/other-run while --fid=../other-run resolves to docs/plans/202610/other-run, so its no-deferral-row check passes even with the guard removed

A climbing `--fid=../../../..` passed to `bkit runs gate --validated`, `bkit runs revalidate` or `bkit workflows handover --push|--flush` still makes the merge gate treat a source change as bookkeeping-only, or sweeps the whole tree into a commit pushed to `dev`, because the new check guards three handlers and not the `checkOnlyBookkeeping` / `commitBookkeeping` sinks

A refused `bkit ledgers commit`, `bkit ledgers only-bookkeeping` or `bkit decisions pending` with `--fid=../../202610/logs/other-run` still appends an `engine-call` row to that other run's `status.jsonl`, because the dispatcher's journal resolves the raw `--fid` into a path before the handler's check runs

challengeFindings.title: A `--month=*` passed to `bkit runs gate --validated` or `bkit runs revalidate` is still accepted and widens the FID's bookkeeping allow-list to every month bucket, because `checkOnlyBookkeeping` grants the CI hook's wildcard exemption to every caller

`bkit ledgers commit --path='*' --mode=commit` (or `--path=':(top)'`, `--path='docs/*.md'`) sweeps every changed and untracked file in the checkout into one bookkeeping commit, because `commitOnePath` hands the `--path` value to `git add --` and `git commit --` as a pathspec pattern, not a literal path; this is the same widening the build closes for `--fid`, on the same command
